predecessors.name: Huns
predecessors.text: the kingdom 'north of the Danube' bordering the Rugians on the Danube: 'southern Moravia or southwestern Slovakia' (many scholars)

successors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
successors.text: the land 'near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia' given by Justinian 'after he became emperor in 527': the Roman side, south of the Sava and the Danube

ledger.x: 460: the Heruli consolidate a kingdom on the Middle Danube.
491: the Heruli make the Lombards pay tribute.
494: Rodulf attacks the Lombards and the tribute ends.
512: the Heruli cross the Danube into the Roman Empire.
512: the Heruli become Roman federates in the Balkans.
After 527: Justinian gives land near Singidunum.
After 527: the Singidunum land is held as a Roman federate colony; the year is the grant's lower bound, as in the 527 gain.
539: the Bassianae district leaves the Roman federation: the Gepid dossier holds all of it from 539.
539: the Bassianae district passes to the Gepids.

wars.name: Battle of Bolia
wars.outcome: Ostrogothic victory 'achieving supremacy in Pannonia'; the Heruli are listed in the opposing coalition.

wars.name: Herulian-Lombard war
wars.outcome: Rodulf attacks the Lombards in 494 and is killed; the Heruli kingdom ends (Procopius); Paul the Deacon puts it between 494 and 511.

wars.name: Theoderic's campaign against the Heruli
wars.outcome: Ennodius's panegyric indicates Theoderic's forces killed 'large numbers of Heruli' at their own settlements after an attack on Theoderic.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for either phase; the Danubian kingdom is placed by the disputed readings of Procopius (three admin1 units north of the Danube), the Balkan colony by two place names (Bassianae, Singidunum) drawn as a district and…
